Photorealism is beautiful in games

Photorealism is beautiful in games

The trouble is that any game aiming to be photorealistic ages like milk, as future graphics will make it look like shit in restrospective. Highly stylized, drawn and pixel graphics age better, and some of them (like Out of this World) have remained aesthetically timeless despite technical advances for their unique art style.

I've found that they age at roughly the same rate regardless of "style" (unless it's ASCII). It's more about how it's pulled off rather than photorealism vs stylized. For example, the old "I Spy" games, or FMV sequences visually hold up about as well as OotW; the visual techniques at play are unorthodox, but it's still photorealism. Don't know if you'd qualify Serious Sam as photorealism (it's closer to real than stylized I guess), but the original holds up quite well visually, especially in motion. Also, we've surpassed a point a few years ago where photorealism doesn't age like shit anymore, compared to its earlier days. I think the source of this meme is that "stylized" is often 2D, whereas "real" often goes for 3D. The latter is obviously more inclined to age poorly. 2D games attempting photorealism hold up a lot more easily than 3D stylized games.

Hell, the graphics cards of that day only had around 64Mb of DDR memory.

That being said, Deus Ex was greater than the sum of its parts. The individual pieces weren't great alone, but once you put them together in the way Eidos did, fuck yeah it was great. When Revision came out, I was super excited, I played quite a bit out of it.
